problem_statement:
Cloudflare Web Analytics beacon gets injected into Carrel's private HTML pages

Carrel is private, but Cloudflare's automatic Web Analytics injection still edits its HTML responses on the way out, adding the beacon script to pages behind the Access gate and to the AI door's OAuth consent page. (Excluding the hostnames in the dashboard needs a paid plan, and the strict CSP should not be loosened for the beacon.) Cloudflare leaves a response alone when its Cache-Control says `no-transform`, but Carrel's responses never say that.

Reproduce: pass any HTML response through the gate (`workers/gate.ts`) for an admitted user, or open the OAuth authorize page of the MCP door. The gate response has `Cache-Control: private, no-store` and the consent page has `Cache-Control: no-store`.

Expected:
- HTML responses passed through the gate (Content-Type starting with `text/html`, compared case-insensitively) carry a single `Cache-Control: private, no-store, no-transform` header.
- Non-HTML responses (CSS, JavaScript, fonts, JSON, plain text) keep `private, no-store`, so they remain compressible.
- The door's OAuth consent page is sent with `Cache-Control: no-store, no-transform`.
fail_to_pass: npx vitest run test/access.test.ts -t "leaves an HTML page untransformed"
npx vitest run test/door.test.ts -t "an Owner signs in, and the grant reaches the tools as that person"
pass_to_pass: npx vitest run test/access.test.ts -t "matches the email without regard to case"
